issues.body: `_NEEDS_REF_RE` recognizes only `needs.<job>.`, but GitHub expressions also permit index/property access such as `needs['queue-validated'].outputs.foo`. Adding a push-skip conjunct in that form would not change `got`, so `test_push_chain_guards_gain_no_undeclared_needs_gate` would remain green. The behavioral assertions do not close this hole: their synthetic contexts omit the new dependency, which is precisely why this PR adds a structural check. This contradicts the load-bearing claim that every new `needs.*` gate is pinned and leaves the silent post-merge skip path unprotected.
issues.fix_hint: Parse all valid GitHub expression property/index forms when extracting references (including quoted bracket access), or conservatively reject any `needs` access that cannot be fully classified. Add a mutation-style test using a bracket-indexed undeclared dependency and assert that the structural validator rejects it.
issues.title: Needs-reference pin can be bypassed with valid bracket syntax

verdict.summary: The new tests improve coverage of the current push-to-main chain, but the structural guard-reference check does not actually enforce its stated invariant for all valid GitHub Actions expressions. A future push skip can use bracket-indexed `needs` syntax and bypass the regex while the synthetic evaluator also treats the absent dependency in a way that can leave the behavioral assertions green. Because this is the exact silent-skip class the change claims to prevent, the test is incomplete.
